name: Vancouver
tagline: Mountains, sea and rainforest framing a glass city.
bestMonths: May, Jun, Jul, Aug and Sep
whenBlurb: Come June to September for dry, glorious days on ocean and mountain; time spring for cherry blossom and whale season, and expect grey rain the rest of the year.

ourTake.lede: Vancouver rewards the traveller who treats the city as a base rather than the destination, the mountains, the ocean and the islands are where it comes alive. Give downtown a night or two, then point yourself at Stanley Park, the North Shore and the water. Skip the aquarium-and-Gastown-clock circuit; spend that time on Granville Island early, before the tour groups.
ourTake.comeIf: You want mountains, ocean and forest at the edge of a relaxed city, with Whistler close by.
ourTake.skipIf: You want guaranteed sun outside summer or a fast, urban-only break.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Fairmont Pacific Rim
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Five-Star (2025), hotel and spa
items.description: Vancouver's defining modern grand hotel, glass and art above the harbour, faced to the sea and the mountains beyond.

items.name: Rosewood Hotel Georgia
items.description: A restored 1927 landmark of old-Hollywood glamour, dark wood, a saltwater infinity pool, and the city's most storied address.

items.name: Shangri-La Vancouver
items.description: The city's tallest tower turned discreet luxury house, spacious rooms, Asian calm, MO-standard service.

items.name: Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
items.description: A family-owned European jewel on Robson Square, antiques, Persian rugs, and Vancouver's most personal service.

items.name: Loden Hotel
items.description: A polished boutique hideaway on the quiet edge of Coal Harbour, mid-century calm with harbour and mountain light.

items.name: The Douglas, Autograph Collection
items.description: A design-led tower rising from the Parq entertainment complex, warm cedar, mountain views, and a private urban garden.

items.name: Fairmont Hotel Vancouver
items.description: The green-roofed 'Castle in the City' since 1939, a chateau-style landmark at the heart of downtown.

items.name: Pan Pacific Vancouver
credentials: Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards 2025 (Best Hotels in Canada)
items.description: Perched over Canada Place under the white sails, the definitive harbour-front address, ships and seaplanes at the door.

items.name: JW Marriott Parq Vancouver
items.description: The polished flagship of the Parq complex, contemporary rooms above a rooftop park and a cluster of restaurants.

items.name: Stanley Park Seawall
items.description: A 9-kilometre paved rim traces the peninsula between old-growth forest and the sea, past the Lions Gate Bridge, English Bay and the downtown skyline. Have your guide arrange a private cycle or a slow morning stroll before the crowds; grandparents and children keep the same flat, car-free path.

items.name: Brockton Point Totem Poles
items.description: Nine towering First Nations poles stand in a meadow near the water, some carved as early as the 1880s and among the most-photographed sights in British Columbia. A small interpretive centre explains the Kwakwaka'wakw and Haida stories behind them, a gentle first read on Indigenous culture for a multi-generation group.

items.name: Prospect Point
items.description: The high bluff at the park's north tip looks straight onto the Lions Gate Bridge and the Burrard Inlet, with a cafe and gift shop for a pause. It is the classic photo-stop on a private drive around the park.

items.name: Vancouver Aquarium
items.description: Set inside Stanley Park, Canada's largest aquarium runs sea otters, jellies and a rainforest gallery that reliably holds young children for hours. A calm, indoor option when the coast turns grey.

items.name: Lost Lagoon
items.description: A tranquil freshwater lake at the park's edge, ringed by a level trail where herons and swans gather at dusk. A quiet, unhurried loop for grandparents who want the park without the full seawall.

items.name: Granville Island Public Market
items.description: An indoor food hall under the Granville Bridge where farm stalls, Oyama Sausage, Benton Brothers cheese and Belgian chocolatiers sit beside fresh-off-the-boat seafood. A private tasting walk here is the easiest, most delicious hour in the city, with plenty for vegetarians.

items.name: Granville Island artisan studios & galleries
items.description: Beyond the market, the island's converted warehouses hold glass-blowers, potters, a sake maker and independent galleries. A relaxed browse for a collector, walkable and free of traffic.

items.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
items.description: A 137-metre cable bridge sways 70 metres above the Capilano River canyon, with a Treetops walk strung between 1,300-year-old Douglas firs and a glass Cliffwalk cantilevered off the rock. The engineered thrill everyone photographs; a private driver spares you the North Shore parking scrum.

items.name: Grouse Mountain
credentials: Eye of the Wind, a glass viewing pod set just below the blades of a working wind turbine, billed as the only one of its kind.
items.description: The Skyride gondola climbs to an alpine playground with 360-degree city and ocean views, a resident pair of grizzlies named Grinder and Coola, a lumberjack show and the Eye of the Wind turbine you can stand beneath. A single mountain that fills a whole family day, dawn to dusk.

items.name: Lynn Canyon Park & Suspension Bridge
items.description: A free 50-metre suspension bridge over a rainforest gorge with waterfalls and swimming holes, the local's quieter answer to Capilano. Bring a private guide and you get temperate rainforest with none of the ticket-gate crowds.

items.name: Gastown & the Steam Clock
items.description: Vancouver's oldest quarter, all cobblestones and Victorian brick, anchored by the whistling steam clock that puffs Westminster chimes on the quarter-hour. Boutiques, First Nations galleries and some of the city's best restaurants line the same few blocks.

items.name: Chinatown
items.description: One of North America's largest historic Chinatowns, with the ornate Millennium Gate, herbalists and a growing wave of new restaurants and bars. Best explored on foot with a guide who can read the layers of old and new.

items.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
credentials: The first authentic classical Chinese garden built outside of China, opened in 1986.
items.description: A walled Ming Dynasty scholar's garden of jade water, limestone and pavilions, the first full classical Chinese garden built outside China. A pocket of stillness in the middle of the city, marking its 40th year in 2026.

items.name: Museum of Anthropology at UBC
credentials: Home to the world's largest collection of works by Haida artist Bill Reid.
items.description: Arthur Erickson's soaring Great Hall of glass and concrete frames towering totem poles, canoes and works from Haida, Nisga'a and Coast Salish nations, reopened in 2024 after a seismic rebuild. It holds the world's largest collection of Bill Reid, including his masterwork The Raven and the First Men.

items.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
credentials: Holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr's work.
items.description: The city's flagship gallery, beside Robson Square, holds the world's most important collection of Emily Carr, the painter of British Columbia's forests and Indigenous villages. Through 2026 it shows its largest Carr exhibition in over twenty years.

items.name: Canada Place & the waterfront
items.description: The white sail-roofed cruise pier juts into Burrard Inlet with a seawall promenade, the Canadian Trail interpretive walk and float planes taking off from the harbour. An easy, level introduction to the city's water-meets-mountains setting.

items.name: FlyOver Canada
items.description: A flight-simulator ride inside Canada Place that suspends you before a 20-metre dome screen and sweeps you coast to coast with wind, mist and scent. Eight thrilling minutes that delight children and grandparents alike, whatever the weather outside.

items.name: Science World
items.description: The mirrored geodesic dome at the head of False Creek, built for Expo 86, is a hands-on science centre with an OMNIMAX dome theatre and floors of experiments for curious kids. Its 391 lights run programmed sequences over the water every night.

items.name: English Bay Beach
items.description: The city's most beloved downtown beach, where locals gather for sunsets over the freighters and the summer fireworks. Steps from West End restaurants, an easy stroll for an evening with the family.

items.name: Kitsilano Beach
items.description: A wide sandy beach backed by lawns, tennis courts and Vancouver's landmark 137-metre saltwater pool, framed by mountain and skyline views. The heart of laid-back "Kits", ringed by good cafes and yoga-set shops.

items.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
items.description: A former rock quarry transformed into the city's most-visited park, crowning Vancouver's highest point with formal flower gardens and a panorama of downtown against the North Shore mountains. A gentle, manicured green space for a slow multi-generation afternoon.

items.name: Bloedel Conservatory
items.description: A glass dome atop Queen Elizabeth Park holding tropical, subtropical and desert zones under one roof, with free-flying parrots and koi. A warm, colourful refuge on a rainy day, small enough not to tire anyone.

items.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
items.description: A 22-hectare garden of 7,500 plant species across sixty themed sections, with an Elizabethan hedge maze and a striking undulating-roof visitor centre. Serene and never crowded, ideal for a private morning wander.

items.name: Lonsdale Quay & the SeaBus crossing
items.description: Ride the SeaBus twelve minutes across the harbour for one of the great cheap skyline views, landing at a lively public market and the neon Shipyards district. A short, scenic outing that feels like a proper voyage to the children.

items.name: Commercial Drive
items.description: The city's old Italian quarter, now a bohemian stretch of espresso bars, patios and independent shops known simply as "The Drive". A neighbourhood to wander for anyone who wants the real, unpolished Vancouver.

items.name: Punjabi Market (Little India)
items.description: The stretch of Main Street between 49th and 51st that has been Vancouver's Little India since the 1970s, with sari shops, sweet houses and institutions like the Himalaya Restaurant. A nostalgic, homely detour for Indian families, quieter now that much of the community has moved to Surrey.

items.name: Surrey & the South Asian food belt
items.description: Home to one of the largest Punjabi communities outside India, Surrey's Newton and Payal Business Centre serve the region's most authentic Punjabi, Gujarati and South Indian cooking, plus gurdwaras and sweet shops. Worth a private car trip for a homesick, food-loving multi-gen group.

items.name: Aberdeen Centre & the Golden Village
items.description: Richmond's Golden Village is one of North America's densest concentrations of Asian malls and restaurants, with Aberdeen Centre's food court and bubble-tea culture the anchor. A vegetarian-friendly, kid-pleasing crash course in Hong Kong and Taiwanese food.

items.name: Richmond Night Market
credentials: The largest night market in North America.
items.description: The largest night market in North America, over a hundred stalls and 500-plus dishes of hawker-style Asian street food under strings of lights, running weekend evenings from spring to September. A festive, sensory night out for all ages; a private driver makes the far-out location painless.

items.name: Steveston Village
items.description: A historic fishing village where you can buy salmon and crab straight off the boats at Fisherman's Wharf, tour a heritage cannery and stroll a boardwalk to the river's mouth. A charming, low-key half-day with genuine maritime character.

items.name: Sea-to-Sky Gondola
items.description: A ten-minute climb above Howe Sound to a summit lodge with a viewing platform, a suspension bridge and alpine trails looking over turquoise fjord water. The quieter, more natural alternative to Whistler's Peak 2 Peak, an hour up the coast.

items.name: Sea-to-Sky Highway drive
items.description: One of the world's great coastal drives, hugging the Howe Sound fjord from Vancouver past Shannon Falls and Squamish up to Whistler. With a private driver it becomes a leisurely day of turnouts, waterfalls and photographs rather than a slog.

items.name: Shannon Falls
items.description: British Columbia's third-highest waterfall at 335 metres, a short flat walk from the Sea-to-Sky Highway to a viewing platform in the spray. A five-minute stop that feels like a proper wilderness moment.

items.name: Whistler Village
items.description: A pedestrian alpine resort of cobbled lanes, patios and boutiques ninety minutes north, framed by two ski mountains and buzzing summer and winter alike. The natural base for a mountain day, or an overnight for a longer stay.

items.name: Peak 2 Peak Gondola
credentials: Holds the Guinness record for highest cable car above ground, at 436 metres, and among the longest unsupported spans between two towers, at just over three kilometres.
items.description: A glass-floored gondola glides between Whistler and Blackcomb mountains, hanging 436 metres above the valley across a single record-setting span, with the Peak Suspension Bridge at the top. The showstopper mountain experience for a group out to be wowed.

items.name: Victoria & the Inner Harbour
items.description: British Columbia's genteel capital, reached by ferry or floatplane, wraps its harbour with the ivy-clad Fairmont Empress and the domed Parliament Buildings, made for afternoon tea and a slow waterfront wander. A full day, or better an overnight, paired with Butchart Gardens.

items.name: The Butchart Gardens
credentials: Designated a National Historic Site of Canada.
items.description: A 55-acre floral masterpiece near Victoria, built inside a spent limestone quarry, whose Sunken Garden is among the most celebrated garden spaces in the world. A National Historic Site, still family-owned after 120-plus years, spectacular whatever the season.

items.name: Bowen Island
items.description: A twenty-minute ferry from Horseshoe Bay lands you at Snug Cove, an artist's island of cafes, galleries, sandy coves and fifty kilometres of forest trails with no chain in sight. Vancouver's closest island escape, easy and unhurried for a half-day.

items.name: Cypress Mountain lookout
items.description: A short mountain drive above West Vancouver ends at a lookout that takes in the whole city, the Gulf Islands and, on a clear day, Mount Baker across the border. The best sunset panorama within twenty minutes of downtown.

items.name: Deep Cove
items.description: A postcard cove tucked into the fjord where you can rent a kayak on calm water, walk the Quarry Rock trail for a view, and reward the effort with a famous Honey's doughnut. A gentle, pretty morning off the tourist trail.

items.name: Nitobe Memorial Garden
items.description: A serene Japanese stroll-and-tea garden on the UBC campus, considered one of the most authentic outside Japan, with a tea house, koi and maples that blaze in autumn. A meditative counterpoint to the nearby Museum of Anthropology.

items.name: Grouse Grind trail
items.description: A relentless 2.9-kilometre staircase up the face of Grouse Mountain, known as "Mother Nature's Stairmaster", that fit visitors climb before riding the gondola back down. For the athletic member of the party who wants a real challenge with a view.

items.name: Second Beach & Ceperley Meadow
items.description: A family beach on the Stanley Park seawall with a heated outdoor pool, a playground and a big grassy meadow for a picnic. The easiest spot to let children loose while adults take in the sea view.

items.name: Vancouver Lookout at Harbour Centre
items.description: A glass elevator shoots up to a 360-degree observation deck 168 metres over downtown, taking in the harbour, Stanley Park and the mountains in one turn. The quickest way to orient a group on their first day.

items.name: Robson Street shopping
items.description: The city's flagship shopping promenade, running from the art gallery toward Stanley Park, mixing global luxury names with cafes and people-watching patios. The obvious stroll for a retail afternoon downtown.

items.name: Mount Seymour
items.description: The least-visited of the three North Shore peaks, a quieter drive up to alpine meadows, easy family trails in summer and gentle ski slopes in winter, all with a broad valley view. The insider's choice when Grouse feels too busy.

items.name: Yaletown
items.description: A former warehouse district turned polished waterfront neighbourhood of loading-dock patios, design shops and marina views onto False Creek. The stylish quarter for an evening of dinner and a stroll along the seawall.

items.name: Masayoshi
items.description: Masayoshi Baba's serene sushi counter, exacting edomae craft away from the downtown crowds.

items.name: Okeya Kyujiro
items.description: A theatrical kaiseki-and-sushi experience under lantern light, dining as performance.

items.name: Sushi Hyun
items.description: A minimalist omakase counter of great purity, fish flown in and treated with reverence.

items.name: Sushi Masuda
items.description: A Tokyo-trained master's edomae counter, classical sushi of quiet, uncompromising standard.

items.name: AnnaLena
items.description: Playful, precise contemporary cooking in a warm West-Side room, Vancouver at its most confidently modern.

items.name: Barbara
items.description: A tiny, ingredient-obsessed counter in Chinatown, a personal tasting menu of quiet intensity.

items.name: Burdock & Co
items.description: Andrea Carlson's seasonal, farm-driven cooking, Pacific Northwest terroir on a plate.

items.name: iDen & QuanJuDe Beijing Duck House
items.description: The famed Beijing duck house brought to Vancouver, lacquered Peking duck of real ceremony.

items.name: Kissa Tanto
items.description: A moody, 1960s-Tokyo-jazz-bar room serving singular Japanese-Italian cooking, one of the city's most-loved tables.

items.name: Published on Main
items.description: The city's most celebrated modern room, refined, seasonal cooking on buzzing Main Street.

items.name: St. Lawrence
items.description: A Québécois-French bistro dressed as a Montréal railway diner, hearty, exact, deeply comforting.

items.name: Sumibiyaki Arashi
items.description: An intimate charcoal-grill counter, yakitori and sumibiyaki cooked with quiet precision.

items.name: Botanist
items.description: Modern Canadian cooking inside the Fairmont Pacific Rim, polished, seasonal, and beautifully served.

items.name: Vij's
items.description: Vikram Vij's landmark of modern Indian cooking, the restaurant that reimagined Indian food in Canada.

items.name: Karma Indian Bistro
items.description: Refined, generous Indian cooking that earned Michelin's value nod, warm and familiar for Indian palates.

items.name: Anh and Chi
items.description: Beloved, beautifully run modern Vietnamese on Main, family-owned and full of heart.

items.name: Phnom Penh
items.description: The legendary Cambodian-Vietnamese room, its butter beef and chicken wings are a Vancouver rite of passage.

items.name: Fable Kitchen
items.description: Honest farm-to-table cooking on West 4th, rustic, seasonal and consistently good.

items.name: Good Thief
items.description: An inventive, value-driven room that won Michelin's newest nod on Main, bold and unexpected.

items.name: The Lunch Lady
items.description: A Vancouver homage to Saigon's famous street-food matriarch, bright, punchy Vietnamese.

items.name: 1927 Lobby Lounge, Rosewood Hotel Georgia
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key hotel, a restored 1927 landmark
items.description: A jewel-box hotel lounge under the restored 1927 ceiling, the city's most glamorous nightcap.

items.name: Bacchus, Wedgewood Hotel & Spa
credentials: Inside a Relais & Châteaux, MICHELIN One-Key hotel
items.description: A clubby, wood-panelled piano bar in a Relais & Châteaux house, Vancouver's most European nightcap.

items.name: Botanist Bar
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 26), highest Vancouver entry
items.description: The bar inside Vancouver's only Forbes Five-Star hotel, botanically-driven cocktails and the city's highest-ranked drinking room.

items.name: The Keefer Bar
credentials: Named Best Bar in Canada on the 2025 list
items.description: An apothecary-themed cocktail den inspired by Chinatown's historic herbalists, dark, aromatic and thrilling.

items.name: Prophecy
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 53, extended list)
items.description: A refined, low-lit cocktail room bringing serious drinks and hospitality to Gastown, a rising Vancouver name.

items.name: Meo
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 92, extended list)
items.description: An inventive, intimate cocktail bar with a devoted following, one of the city's newest 50-Best names.

items.name: Reflections, The Rooftop, The Douglas
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Guide selected hotel, a seasonal urban-garden rooftop
items.description: A garden terrace above the Parq complex, fire pits, greenery and open-air drinks over the city.

items.name: Laowai
credentials: North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 67, extended list)
Named Best New Bar in Canada (2022)
items.description: A hidden 1920s-Shanghai speakeasy behind a freezer door, velvet, brass and glamour, and drinks to match.

plan.heading: 3 days in Vancouver, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Settle into the Fairmont Pacific Rim, then cycle or walk the Stanley Park seawall.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Granville Island's market and makers, lunch by the water.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Published on Main in Mount Pleasant, the city's tasting-menu leader.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A private drive up the Sea-to-Sky Highway to Squamish and the Sea to Sky Gondola.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Whistler village or a return along Howe Sound with a stop at Britannia.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Kissa Tanto in Chinatown for its Italian-Japanese kitchen.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Museum of Anthropology at UBC for its Northwest Coast collection.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The Capilano suspension bridge or a quieter walk at Lynn Canyon.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Omakase at Masayoshi in Kerrisdale to close the visit.

items.name: Coal Harbour
items.description: Glassy waterfront near Stanley Park and the seaplane terminal; the easy choice for a first stay.

items.name: Yaletown
items.description: Converted-warehouse blocks with the best restaurants and marina; suits those who want to walk to dinner.

items.name: Kitsilano
items.description: Beachy, low-rise and relaxed across the water; for travellers who want mornings by the sea, not the towers.

events.name: Vancouver International Wine Festival
events.note: The city's serious oenophile week, with a themed region and a large public tasting hall.

events.name: Vivid, Celebration of Light (fireworks)
events.note: Barge-launched international fireworks competition over English Bay across several nights.

events.name: Vancouver International Film Festival
events.note: One of North America's larger festivals, strong on Asian and Canadian cinema.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Stay in Coal Harbour or the West End for water and mountain views; it rains often outside summer, so waterproofs matter, and the drive to Whistler along the Sea-to-Sky highway is worth a full day.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Arrive into Vancouver International (YVR), about 30 minutes from downtown; a private car handles the transfer, or a floatplane can land you on the harbour beside Coal Harbour.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver suits the mountains-and-sea geography and day trips to Whistler; downtown, Stanley Park and Coal Harbour are pleasant on foot.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Canadian eSIMs activate instantly; wifi is fast throughout.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Canadian dollars; cards and contactless everywhere; tip 18–20 percent in restaurants.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: July to September is dry, mild and luminous, with the mountains and sea at their best; November to February is grey and persistently wet, atmospheric, but not the trip to book for sun.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Air India flies Delhi to Vancouver direct, roughly 15-16 hours, comfortable in business; Air Canada also runs nonstop. Alternatively one stop via the Gulf (Emirates, Qatar) or a Pacific routing through Hong Kong (Cathay), all strong up front, with fine lounges to break the journey.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations required; tap water is pristine. Very safe; only routine caution, and note the visible tents and drug scene around parts of the Downtown Eastside, which is easily skirted. Rain, not risk, is the planning factor.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain needs are handled with ease across the city. A large South Asian community, especially in Surrey, means authentic and abundant Indian food, pure-veg thalis, chaat and South Indian are never far.
